repo_description: Proof and publication materials for local-memory costs of explicit termination in anonymous dynamic binary consensus.
title: Internal Time as Local Memory: Explicit Termination in Anonymous Dynamic Binary Consensus
abstract: We study deterministic binary consensus in anonymous synchronous 1-interval-connected dynamic networks under one-bit broadcast-counting communication. The paper compares three ways of certifying that enough information-propagation time has elapsed. Stabilization is size-oblivious and needs exactly one bit of persistent local state. In the clockless model, explicit termination has logarithmic local-memory cost: if the network size n is known non-uniformly, then M_term^size(n)=Theta(log n); if n is unknown but a common temporal dissemination bound (dynamic diameter) D is known non-uniformly, then M_term^diam(D)=Theta(log(D+1)). Both lower bounds follow from a common split-cycle indistinguishability plus finite-state pumping argument, and matching upper bounds use one-bit flooding plus an internal counter. If the global round number is supplied for free as an external input, known-D explicit termination uses only constant persistent memory. Thus the logarithmic termination memory represents elapsed-time evidence rather than the consensus value itself. The claimed contribution is restricted to these local-space characterizations and their comparison; flooding, locality, dynamic-diameter notions, and finite-state pumping are standard.
